# Callouts: Flash backup 10.11 - U7's reset (pin 35) and where to hold it

Source: Own photos, raptox's unit: stitched microscope mosaic of 2026-11-03 (229 px/mm, full resolution)  
Annotated image: [images/annotated/fb10-4_cooker-u7-reset.jpg](../../../images/annotated/fb10-4_cooker-u7-reset.jpg)

Pin 35 (RESET_N) runs left and down to the top pad of the tan 0402 part (2), `likely` its reset capacitor to GND. Held to GND there, U7 stays in reset and lets go of the serial lines it shares with the Wi-Fi chip. Beep first: 1 to 2 beeps, 3 to GND beeps, 2 to 3V3 must NOT beep.

| # | Ref | Identification | Part / marking | Category | Confidence | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | U7.35 | RESET_N | CC2640R2F | MCU / SoC | likely | Pin 35 (SWRS204C p. 9: no internal pull-up), the 11th pin of the left row from the top, 2nd from the bottom (picture 10.1). Its trace leaves the toe up-left, then runs down to 2. |
| 2 | C?.1 | the hold point: GND probe here | 0402, tan (a capacitor) | Debug / programming / test | likely | The pad pin 35's trace ends on (mosaic). Beep to pin 35 first, and check it does NOT beep to 3V3 (U15 pin 8). Then a GND probe here, before power, as on TP33. |
| 3 | C?.2 | the other pad: GND? |  | Power | guess | If it beeps to GND, the part is the reset capacitor and 2 is safe to hold low. |
| 4 | R? | not this one (pin 36's trace) | 0402, black (a resistor) | Marking / label | guess | Pin 36's (DIO_23) trace runs down to its top pad (mosaic). |
